red_flags.clinical_rationale: Systolic BP <90 mmHg with severe tachycardia (HR >130) indicates cardiogenic shock or massive PE requiring immediate resuscitation over diagnostic workup. Present in all four conditions at their most severe. Source: McCullough 2002 (CHF), Kline 2008 PERC rule (PE).
red_flags.halt_message: ⚠ HAEMODYNAMIC COLLAPSE detected. Differential diagnosis deferred. Immediate interventions required: IV fluid resuscitation, vasopressor support, urgent cardiology consultation.

red_flags.clinical_rationale: Syncope (indicating acute RV strain/reduced cardiac output) combined with hypoxia (SpO2 <88%) and tachycardia defines massive PE per Kline 2008 and Geneva score criteria. Requires emergency thrombectomy or thrombolysis, not diagnostic workup. Source: Kline 2008, Klok 2008 (Geneva score).
red_flags.halt_message: ⚠ MASSIVE PE suspected (syncope + severe hypoxia + tachycardia). Differential diagnosis deferred. Activate emergency thrombectomy/thrombolysis protocol; urgent CT angiography and interventional cardiology.

red_flags.display_name: Acute Coronary Syndrome with Active Ischaemia
red_flags.clinical_rationale: ST elevation on ECG or ongoing severe chest pain with positive troponin indicates acute myocardial infarction requiring emergency reperfusion (PCI/thrombolysis), not diagnostic workup for UA/stable conditions. Overlaps with UA scope but demands immediate intervention. Source: Bruyninckx 2008 (UA/ACS definition).

triggers.description: ST elevation ≥1 mm in contiguous leads

red_flags.halt_message: ⚠ ACUTE ST-ELEVATION MI detected. Differential diagnosis deferred. Activate STEMI protocol: emergency ECG, troponin, urgent cardiology, reperfusion therapy (PCI or thrombolysis).

red_flags.display_name: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure with Pulmonary Oedema
red_flags.clinical_rationale: Acute pulmonary oedema (orthopnoea, crackles, hypoxia <88%) indicates end-organ hypoperfusion and respiratory failure. Diagnosis is clear; immediate diuresis, oxygen, and haemodynamic support take priority over differential workup. Source: McCullough 2002 (Breathing Not Properly; N=1538 ED dyspnoea cohort).
red_flags.halt_message: ⚠ ACUTE DECOMPENSATED HEART FAILURE with pulmonary oedema detected. Differential diagnosis deferred. Immediate interventions: high-flow oxygen, IV diuretics, non-invasive ventilation if needed, urgent cardiology.

red_flags.clinical_rationale: Beck's triad (hypotension + elevated JVP + muffled heart sounds) or pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg indicates cardiac tamponade. This is a surgical emergency requiring pericardiocentesis before any diagnostic workup. Source: AFP 2024 (Acute Pericarditis guideline review); tamponade is a known Pericarditis complication.
red_flags.halt_message: ⚠ PERICARDIAL TAMPONADE (Beck's triad) suspected. Differential diagnosis deferred. Emergency bedside echocardiography, prepare for urgent pericardiocentesis; cardiothoracic surgery consultation.
